summary: PulseGuard v0.6.31 fixes the automatic-update bridge from v0.6.30 and includes the complete evidence-first scan, repair and verification improvements.

sections.heading: Automatic update from v0.6.30 is bridge-safe again
sections.detail: The maintenance/recovery logic is integrated into the already-approved main optimizer payload instead of introducing new runtime filenames that the installed v0.6.30 updater rejects. The release therefore fits the v0.6.30 strict file allowlist, while the included updater recognizes the maintenance-engine path for a future controlled split. No manual file copying is required.

sections.heading: Windows integrity and the repair commands are now fully staged
sections.detail: Full Health records DISM /CheckHealth, DISM /ScanHealth and SFC /verifyonly evidence, uses Repair-WindowsImage only as a structured fallback when DISM console text cannot be classified, and records current-session CBS [SR] corroboration. FIX & OPTIMIZE runs DISM /RestoreHealth and SFC /scannow in separate visible elevated windows only for positively repairable corruption, then independently repeats the deep checks before claiming VERIFIED_FIXED. Non-repairable or incomplete diagnostics become REVIEW instead of blind repair, and restart-required servicing becomes REBOOT_REQUIRED until a post-restart deep scan verifies clean.

sections.heading: Filesystem repair is evidence-gated
sections.detail: Full Health uses the dirty bit, volume evidence and CHKDSK /scan. CHKDSK /f runs only when that evidence or an NTFS corruption event justifies it. If the active Windows volume schedules the repair for restart, PulseGuard reports REBOOT_REQUIRED and waits for a later CHKDSK /scan before claiming success.

sections.heading: Targeted DNS repair instead of blind network reset
sections.detail: PulseGuard compares direct-IP TCP connectivity with DNS resolution. ipconfig /flushdns is offered automatically only when direct-IP connectivity works while DNS resolution fails, and DNS is re-tested afterward.

sections.heading: Boot repair commands are recovery-only capabilities
sections.detail: bootrec /fixmbr, bootrec /fixboot, bootrec /rebuildbcd and BCDBoot are mapped under Recovery / Boot but are never executed blindly during an online FIX & OPTIMIZE run. PulseGuard inspects WinRE and the current BCD online and leaves boot rewriting for evidence-gated WinRE/manual escalation.

sections.heading: Windows Update failure recovery is non-destructive
sections.detail: Software/security updates retain per-update ResultCode/HRESULT and SucceededWithErrors is a warning. On a real failure PulseGuard captures Windows Update diagnostics, verifies servicing health, preserves DataStore, Download and catroot2 as timestamped .bak folders, restarts services, verifies the Microsoft Update API, retries once, and rechecks. It does not delete the saved cache or reset Windows Update service ACLs.

sections.heading: Component store and storage maintenance are independently verified
sections.detail: DISM /StartComponentCleanup runs only when /AnalyzeComponentStore recommends it and is followed by another analysis. Storage optimization uses Windows defrag /O so Windows selects media-appropriate handling; any partial volume failure remains REVIEW.

sections.heading: Display and source evidence expanded
sections.detail: GPU inventory now merges Win32_VideoController, present PnP Display devices and signed display-driver evidence. Findings also consume filesystem, WinRE/BCD, VSS, activation, WinGet source, DNS and Windows Update failure-history evidence without creating one tab per command.

sections.heading: Visible sequential maintenance and stronger reports
sections.detail: Repair/update actions that need elevation run one at a time in visible Administrator CMD/PowerShell windows, capture their results, remain visible for five seconds after completion, and then continue. Reports retain the merged display inventory, maintenance results, Windows Update diagnostics/cache preservation/retry evidence, and exact source-stage warnings.

sections.heading: WinGet reliability fixes retained
sections.detail: The WinGet executable-resolution fix remains included: PulseGuard resolves winget.exe as an Application command, passes the absolute executable path into the elevated helper, captures invocation failures, accepts agreements, records output, and detects restart-required results.
